Download a balanced sample of iNaturalist photos

Source: R/benchmark.R
inatPhotos.Rd

Collects field photos to test a key with: for each species, n observations from iNaturalist with an openly licensed photo, the photo files, and a manifest that says where every photo came from, so that a benchmark can be cited and run again.

Usage

inatPhotos(
  taxa,
  n = 20,
  place = NULL,
  qualityGrade = "research",
  licenses = c("cc0", "cc-by", "cc-by-nc"),
  dir,
  fetch = benchInatGet,
  download = benchDownload,
  size = "medium",
  pool = 200,
  strata = 10,
  idBelow = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  perObserver = 1,
  photosPerObservation = 1,
  query = list(),
  pause = 1
)

Arguments

taxa

The species: scientific names, results written "Common name (Genus species)", a dimoose key (its results are used), or iNaturalist taxon ids (a numeric vector, named to give the labels).

n

Observations to sample per species.

place

Optional place to restrict the sample to: an iNaturalist place id, or a name to look up (the best match is used and reported).

qualityGrade

iNaturalist quality grade. "research" means the community agreed on the species.

licenses

Photo licences to accept.

dir

Folder to put the photos and manifest.csv in; one subfolder per species. Keep it outside a package or repository.

fetch

Function function(url, query) that performs an API request and returns the parsed JSON as a list. The default calls the iNaturalist API; tests give their own.

download

Function function(url, destfile) that saves a photo.

size

Photo size: "small" (240 px), "medium" (500 px), "large" (1024 px) or "original".

pool, strata

Size of the pool the sample is drawn from, and the number of slices of the id range it is collected from.

idBelow

Only observations with an id below this; see above.

seed

Seed for drawing the sample from the pool.

perObserver

Most observations to take from one observer per species.

photosPerObservation

Most photos to take from one observation.

query

Further parameters for the observation search, e.g. list(month = "6,7,8") for summer photos only.

pause

Least number of seconds between requests.

Value

The manifest, a data frame with one row per photo: taxon (the label, as given in taxa), scientific_name, taxon_id, observation_id, photo_id, license, attribution, url, observation_url, observed_on, file (relative to dir), quality_grade, place_id, id_below and retrieved; plus path, the full file name on this computer, which is not written to manifest.csv. benchmarkKey() takes it as its photos.

How the sample is drawn

The sample depends only on the arguments, not on the day it is drawn:

  1. idBelow fixes the snapshot: only observations with a smaller id are considered. When it is NULL the newest observation id at the time of the call is used and recorded in the manifest (id_below); give that value to draw the same sample again later.

  2. For each species a pool of up to pool observations is collected from strata equal slices of the id range (the newest observations below each cut), so that the pool spans the years rather than being last month's photos. Ids follow upload dates, so each slice is a short stretch of time and the same stretches are used for every species; raise strata (one request each) for an evener spread over the seasons.

  3. From the pool, sorted by id, n observations are drawn with seed, taking at most perObserver from one observer, so that one person's many photos of the same tree cannot dominate.

Observations that were deleted or lost their research grade since are simply no longer returned, so an old sample can shrink; the photo files already in dir are kept and not downloaded again. A photo that cannot be downloaded, or that turns out not to be an image, is left out of the manifest with a warning; it is not replaced by another.

Which taxon a name means

A name is looked up in iNaturalist's taxon search and must match a taxon's name exactly; a looser match (the search also finds "Oenantheae" and "Oenanthe oenanthe" for "Oenanthe") is never used. A name iNaturalist lists as a synonym resolves to the taxon it now belongs to, with a message. The same name can belong to two taxa (the genus Oenanthe is a bird and a plant): then the one whose rank fits the name best and that has the most observations is used, with a warning that lists the candidates and their ids. Give the taxon id instead of the name to choose yourself. The manifest records the id that was used.

API etiquette

Requests are spaced at least pause seconds apart (iNaturalist asks for about one request a second) and identify themselves with a generic User-Agent. Only photos whose own licence is in licenses are taken; the manifest keeps each photo's licence and attribution, which the CC BY licences require you to show wherever the photos are.

See also

benchmarkKey()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
photos <- inatPhotos(montanaKey(), n = 20, dir = file.path(tempdir(), "inat"))
table(photos$taxon)
} # }
